info.title: MICROSERVICE-apiwizdoc-List Retail Orders Status-v3-spec
info.description: The Retail Orders Status API provides seamless access to the current status of retail orders within the system. By leveraging this endpoint, users can query the status of multiple orders, ensuring they have up-to-date information for order tracking and management. This API is particularly beneficial for retailers, customer service teams, and logistics providers who need to monitor order fulfillment and customer communication effectively. The endpoint streamlines operations by enabling real-time status checks, enhancing overall customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.

get.summary: Retrieve the status of an order.
get.description: This endpoint allows you to fetch the current status of a specific order by its ID. You can use this information to track the progress of the order processing, shipping, and delivery.

requestBody.description: Request body for retrieving the status of orders. This body should contain the necessary parameters to specify the order status query.

200.description: Request completed successfully, returning the current order status.

ListRetailOrdersStatusRequest.description: This schema represents the request body format for retrieving the status of orders through a GET operation. The value is expected to be a string.

status.description: Indicates whether the operation was successful.

referenceNumber.description: A unique identifier for the request or operation.

resultId.description: A unique identifier for the result of the operation.

state.description: The current state of the order.

processingTimeMs.description: The time taken to process the request, in milliseconds.

message.description: A message providing additional information about the operation.

ListRetailOrdersStatusResponse_200.description: Schema representing the response structure for the GET operation to check the status of orders.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user or system that created the order.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the order was created.

automated.description: Indicates whether the order was created automatically.

AuditInfo.description: Schema representing audit information related to the order processing.

x-processing-time.description: Indicates the time taken to process the request, measured in milliseconds. This helps in understanding the efficiency of the operation.
